description: THE BUILT WORLD -- settlements and their buildings, infrastructure, fortifications and works, as the expression of factions and the contents of their holdings. Document 02 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings/. PROPOSED AND HELD BACK IN FULL; nothing ratifies on merge. THE ONTOLOGY: a built thing's FABRIC is a `Site`, its ADDRESS is a `Rung`, and the seam is occupancy, derived rather than stored. This NARROWS ED-IN-0223's *'A BUILDING is a `hearth`'* rather than overturning it -- a building is not a hearth, it STANDS on one, and the hearth is the plot; that is what makes founding expressible and repairs the reading under which a Cathedral had to be a hearth. The licensing argument offered by the design pass (*'breaking a wall would destroy its district'*, via the destroy cascade) WAS FOUND UNSOUND by an antagonist pass -- nothing in the code destroys a Rung or a Site at all -- and the refusal is carried on CARDINALITY instead (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S15). Five site families, each discriminated by which EXISTING table its condition band reaches -- PRODUCER, VESSEL, ENCLOSURE, HALL, DWELLING -- under the rule that a kind reaching no new column is not a new family; as roster rows, never carriers. Note `site_kinds` is `[harbour, seam, body]` today and `body` IS NOT A SITE, so the real baseline is two. FORTIFICATION is an ENCLOSURE `Site` whose CONDITION IS ITS STRENGTH -- bands, not a level -- reading onto three mechanisms that already exist (the mass-battle Walls terrain row when intact; a band refusing a `move` on the contain path, which is the chokepoint; a siege as a contest grading a negative condition delta) with NO siege subsystem, and with the epistemic half that an attacker holds only a decaying claim about the band, so it may never be rendered as fact. HOLDINGS: `commit` makes membership, a `hold` on a Rung makes title, `contain` makes presence, and the footing Queries read across them; `serves:` is world-generation content plus a runtime Query over hold-intersect-commit, never a stored fact about a building. `hold` MUST NOT REACH A `Site` -- confirmed, but NOT for the reason proposed: `share` and `draw_share` are declared RESOLVER-SIDE QUERIES (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md S17), so `share` was never a field and widening `hold` does not make it computable; the ground is that mandatory single-holdership DELETES THE COMMONS, and `share`/`draw_share` being declared-and-unimplemented is the actual `restore` blocker. Because `World.add_tenure` performs no object-class check, that refusal is currently UNENFORCEABLE, so a guard is reported as shipping rather than asked for. THE GHOST POLITY IS LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: engine/season/harness/populated.py writes 16 `hold` Tenures whose subject is a faction Proposition, which ratified Layer 1 and 01_AXIOMS.md's NEVER-list both forbid -- a Layer 1 / Layer 2 contradiction, fixed by keeping the subject a Person and minting the holders. TWO FREE CUTS WERE WITHDRAWN AS BREAKAGES: `fort_level` has live engine readers behind a BLOCKING descriptor export (engine/autoload/game_state.py declares and DERIVES it from garrison -- *'it is a rule, not data, and authoring it would give one number two owners'* -- and tools/registry.py makes `terr.fort_level` a descriptor key), and `facility_tier` is read live by its own registry and set by its loader. MEASURED THIS SESSION, and it reorders the work: after one season on the populated world 37 settlements hold 4810 units of matter and 211 HEARTHS HOLD NONE -- every site hangs from a settlement, every person lives in a hearth, and the shortfall is clamped away silently. So Jordan's provincial-tax cascade needs the crossing built before a policy can condition anything. MATTER's larder and yield steps ARE built; bodies and travel are not; and matter.py's own `not_implemented` decision row is STALE about larders and yield. RECOMMENDATION ON ED-SE-0051, which stays the open escalation: take the CAPACITY arm, as a `capacity(w, rung)` Query over DWELLING sites with a floor and never a fixture -- the decisive argument being that matter-only is not currently a bound at all, because the shortfall is recorded and not acted on. GRADE: `paper` under CLAUDE.md S0.2.

MATTER AND WORKS -- document 04 of proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/. PROPOSED, HELD BACK IN FULL. THE MEASURED PROBLEM, reproducible with `python -m engine.season.harness.populated 2`: after one season on build_realm(0), 37 settlements hold 4,810 units of matter and 211 HEARTHS HOLD NONE -- every one of the 74 sites hangs from a settlement, every one of the 46 persons lives in a hearth, and the shortfall is clamped away silently. Worse: only 13 of the 37 settlements have anyone in their contain subtree at all, holding 1,690 of the 4,810, so the other 3,120 sit where nobody lives. MATTER's larder and yield steps ARE built; bodies and travel are not; and matter.py's own `not_implemented` decision row is STALE about larders and yield. THE ANSWER: matter STAYS where it is produced and moves ONLY by `transfer` -- which preserves AX-1, because a person moves it and `transfer` already conserves -- while eaters DRAW UP the ladder through a new `nearest_store(w, rung, kind)` Query, replacing round one's two content moves. Shortfall crosses the gate into `Person.body` (the matrix row exists and gains its writer), bodies cross `band_floors.person` with the same crossing helper as sites, and death at 0 reuses `_eff_kill`'s cascade as `World.remove_person`. `Rung.envelope` is KEPT as ED-SE-0051's carrier. BUILDING is a `works` Record advanced by `work` whose last stage is `restore` or `found` -- and it costs almost nothing new, because `_eff_create_record` ALREADY mints the Record and opens the maker's `hold`, and matter.py's living-holder test already stops a maturation when the maker is gone, so a works that stalls, is inherited, or dies with its master falls out of shipped code. CARRIED FORWARD from round one because it survived a pessimistic pass: the ontology (a built thing's FABRIC is a Site, its ADDRESS is a Rung -- a building stands on a hearth, and the hearth is the plot), the five site families discriminated by which existing table a condition band reaches, fortification as an ENCLOSURE Site whose CONDITION IS ITS STRENGTH with no siege subsystem, and `hold` NOT reaching a Site because mandatory single-holdership deletes the commons. Also carried: the ontology's original licensing argument was found UNSOUND -- nothing in the tree destroys a Rung or a Site -- so it rests on cardinality; and the `fort_level` and `facility_tier` cuts stay WITHDRAWN as breakages, both having live engine readers behind a blocking descriptor export. ED-SE-0051 STAYS OPEN: the capacity arm is RECOMMENDED, as a `capacity(w, rung)` Query over dwelling sites with a floor and never a fixture, on the ground that matter-only is not currently a bound at all because the shortfall is recorded and not acted on. Per ED-WR-0011 it is answered alongside that row. GRADE: paper.

description: SUPERSEDED IN PART by 04_MATTER_AND_WORKS.md (ED-SE-0053) in proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/. The supersession is PROPOSED and held back in full; this row does not close ED-SE-0052, and it does not touch ED-SE-0051, which stays open as RR-2 with Rung.envelope kept as its carrier. OVERTURNED: the hearth-larder and delivery moves. AUDIT_VERDICT.md limit 3 -- 'the share leaves r.stores at MATTER' contradicts 02_THE_BUILT_WORLD.md's OWN RULED line, since MATTER must not move matter across a contain edge (a tax that collects itself is the fourth clock AX T-c forbids) and transfer binds 'from' to the actor's own containing rung. That correction was already struck into round one during unification; what round two changes is the replacement, which reaches the 211 hearths with NO content move and NO new store. Also overturned: every reading of a built thing gated on in_force, which goes with the carrier. KEPT AND CARRIED FORWARD BY POINTER, not re-argued: the fabric/address ontology; the hold-guard argument; Rung.envelope; the withdrawals of fort_level, facility_tier, governance_modes and power_bases (each verified reader by reader, and the export check is blocking); and section B.4's own FINDING that the wear x restore x yield equilibrium is not player-computable -- the player can intuit direction and not equilibrium, and the repair is interface-side. One correction round one made about itself stands and is worth preserving here because it is the shape of error this repo keeps making: matter.py's TRACE.decision row lists larders and yield as not_implemented and IS STALE -- the larder step runs and the yield step runs, measured at 37 settlements. A comment was quoted as evidence of absence. CLAUDE.md section 0.1 pt 3 names exactly that: to claim X is absent, RUN the thing that would show presence.

24D SUBSTRATE FORK, RULED. `ED-SE-0051`/`RR-2` specifies `capacity(w, rung)` as a Query over 'the rung's dwelling Sites', with a floor, never a fixture table. Measured this session (a read-only planning pass, cross-checked against `harness.populated.build_realm(0)`): ZERO dwelling Sites exist anywhere in the tree. `site_kinds` (`engine/season/rosters.yaml`) is `[harbour, seam, body]` -- `body` is not a site. The 211 things that function as dwellings are `hearth`-kind RUNGS (`populated.py:360-365`), not Sites at all. Two readings were put to Jordan: (a) the literal one -- add a `dwelling` Site kind, mint one per hearth rung, `capacity` queries descendant Sites of that kind; (b) a reinterpretation -- read 'dwelling Sites' as meaning the existing hearth rungs, `capacity` queries hearth-kind descendant rungs instead, no new data family. JORDAN CHOSE (a), THE LITERAL READING, 2026-09-25, in this session, via a structured choice naming both arms and their costs -- accepting a new data family and roughly 211 new Sites in every populated world's content hash, over reinterpreting his own ruling's wording. NOT YET BUILT: this row records the RULING only. Known consequences for whoever builds it, found by the write-up pass that followed: `site_kinds` (`rosters.yaml`) has no `open: true` flag today, so a new kind cannot simply be appended; adding `dwelling` forces `wear_per_season` and `band_floors` rows for it or the fixtures loader raises `Ungraded` (`data/fixtures.py:106-128`); `harness/populated.build_realm` is not the only world-builder -- `harness/corpus_run.py:226-231 build_at` independently mints hearth rungs, so a dwelling-Site minter placed only in `build_realm` leaves every corpus-built world reading the capacity FLOOR rather than a real count, which needs a decision (mint in both builders, or accept the corpus arm as floor-only and say so) before `24d`/`24e` land.
